results.title: Founder smiles increase investor trust and funding | Scientific Reports
results.content: Finally, in a randomized experiment with 51 venture capitalists, we systematically manipulated pitch deck photos to test the causal impact of entrepreneur smiling on investment decisions—including perceived investment opportunity, company valuation, and probability of exit—and demonstrated that this effect is mediated by perceived trustworthiness using fixed-effects regression models. First, based on our within-subjects randomized controlled experiment with venture capitalists, we provide causal evidence that founders’ smiling in pitch materials positively influences funding decisions—including perceived investment opportunity, company valuation, and likelihood of exit—while addressing concerns about the generalizability of prior findings from crowdfunding contexts. Similarly, Study 3, using a within-subjects randomized experiment with 51 professional venture capitalists, initially tested the direct causal effect of founder smiling on investment decisions, and then analyzed trustworthiness as a mediator under experimentally controlled conditions. To test whether trustworthiness mediates the relationship between smiling and funding, we initially conducted a pilot study involving a between-subjects randomized experiment with 210 entrepreneurs and prospective entrepreneurs (described in detail in the Methodology section).
